newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas mostly rangebound, 97/98 contango narrow.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas mostly rangebound, 97/98 contango narrow.

text.p: The UK spot natural gas market saw a slowdown in trade on Wednesday after several busy days, traders and brokers said, although prices for the first quarter next year nudged up after a slight dip on Tuesday.
But with the exception of the first quarter, prices were little changed. "There's been a lot of trading within levels," said a dealer. "It doesn't have much direction now."
The most significant price movement seen was on the differential between the gas years from October 1997 and October 1998.

A contango of around a penny a therm had been seen between the two, with the 1998 year assessed at a premium largely because the Interconnector pipeline between Britain and Belgium opens that October. This is expected to give a boost to prices as gas flows from Britain to higher-priced markets in continental Europe.
But over the last few days prices over this winter and next summer have risen, while the 1998 gas year had been untraded for several days until Wednesday.
As a result, the 1997 gas year appears to have caught up with the later year, and the differential was down to 0.30 pence a therm, with deals done at 13.85 pence in 1997 and 14.15 pence in 1998.

Otherwise there were no surprising movements. One buyer reported buying around 300,000 therms of gas on the day ahead market at between 11.60 pence and 11.75 pence a therm, although no details on volumes, number of trades or prices was given.
The same buyer did some trade on the within-day market in the same prices range, although for much smaller volumes. Again, details were not available.
On the IPE futures market, the long trading drought finally came to an end just before the close of the market.

Thirty lots were done in the fourth quarter at an average price of 14.60 pence a therm. The trades were done four minutes before the close of the contract, and were the first deals since Friday morning.
